name: Temporal, Audit, History, Transactions, and Derived State
purpose: Define cross-domain temporal types/authority, lifecycle-versus-audit evidence, append/correction history, transaction/idempotency rules, stale-revision protection and rebuildable derived-state behavior shared by every Beta 1.0 domain.

decisions.decision: Known application instants persist canonically as UTC whole seconds. Date-only values, durations, unknown effective times and unresolved chronology are represented as distinct temporal types, never fabricated instants.
America/Guayaquil is ordinary operational and fixed SLA calendar authority. User-selected IANA timezone affects only Objective/Task schedule input/presentation/calendar/MW context.
Changing Objective timezone re-renders existing canonical instants; preserving a wall-clock schedule is a separate reviewed reschedule that creates new accepted plan facts.

Source adapters preserve explicit source timezone/offset/profile provenance. Missing or ambiguous chronology remains unresolved rather than using discovery/import/recording/current time as a substitute.
Lifecycle evidence, application audit, proposal/job history and technical diagnostics are separate authorities and combined History views must label their source type.
When an accepted command requires domain mutation, lifecycle evidence and audit, all required authoritative writes commit atomically or all roll back.

Audit rows are application-boundary append-only immutable records inserted exactly once. Idempotency resolves before insertion and duplicate audit identity is an integrity error, never an ignored conflict.

Correction, reversal, cancellation, archival, restoration, supersession, replacement and resend preserve original accepted history and append new exact-target evidence; they do not rewrite prior facts.

Hard deletion is exceptional and only an owning-domain rule may authorize it after dependency validation; required minimized non-reconstructable audit evidence survives where the authority requires it.
Derived projections/caches/materializations are rebuildable and non-authoritative. Recalculation emits no lifecycle event solely because derived state changed.

Commands that depend on mutable facts carry/revalidate base revisions or equivalent preconditions inside the authoritative transaction; stale UI/import/regroup previews cannot commit by last-write-wins.

Cross-domain operations coordinate explicit owning-domain commands under one application transaction where atomicity is required; no module directly mutates another domain's tables to simulate orchestration.
